The Federal Government has threatened to prosecute manufacturers and traders found selling underweight products or using faulty weighing and measuring equipment, warning that offenders who repeatedly violate the law will face legal action. The Director of the Weights and Measures Department, Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment, Mr Salim Mohammed, gave the warning during a market surveillance exercise at a supermarket in Lagos on Friday. Mohammed said the department had established tolerance levels for weighing and measuring equipment and prepackaged products in line with international standards, adding that any product or equipment found outside the acceptable range would be withdrawn from sale or taken out of use. He explained that while the department usually issued warnings and notices of rejection to first-time offenders, repeated violations could lead to prosecution. “All measurements are subject to errors and uncertainty. This is why the government, through the Weights and Measures Department, adopts standards based on international studies, standards and practices, particularly those established by the International Organisation of Legal Metrology, to which Nigeria belongs. “If the equipment falls outside the acceptable tolerance level, we immediately prohibit its use. Similarly, if a product being sold does not meet the prescribed tolerance, we direct the seller to remove it from the shelves. “However, where the violation is repeated, the matter may be escalated to the point of prosecution,” he said. The director disclosed that the department recorded over 90 per cent compliance during its inspections, adding that operators whose weighing equipment passed verification were issued certificates valid for 12 months. Mohammed said equipment that failed verification would be labelled unfit for use, while operators would be issued notices of rejection and required to rectify the faults before another verification exercise. The director said the department’s enforcement activities covered the oil and gas and non-oil sectors, including supermarkets, bakeries, open markets, manufacturing facilities and filling stations. Mohammed said the department had prosecuted offenders in Taraba, Jigawa, Oyo, Sokoto and Katsina states, stressing that prosecution remained the last resort for operators who refused to comply with regulations. Cordelia said the department would contact the company over the affected product, stressing that consumers deserved to get the exact quantity stated on the packaging. She urged consumers who suspected that they had been short-changed when purchasing goods or services to report their complaints to the department. She listed filling stations, gas companies, supermarkets, open markets, butcher shops and manufacturing companies among the sectors covered by the inspections. She said, “Consumers in Lagos who feel they have been short-changed in any sector can report such cases to our office. This covers the oil and gas sector, including filling stations and gas companies, supermarkets, open markets, butcher shops and manufacturing companies. “For instance, if you buy food items such as semovita and suspect that the quantity does not correspond with the stated weight, you can verify it with a weighing scale at home. If you discover that a product labelled 10kg weighs less than that, you can report the matter to our office. “We have two offices in Lagos: one in Ijora and the other in Ikeja. Consumers can report their complaints at either location, depending on their proximity.” Meanwhile, the inspection team also visited TotalEnergies in the Kirikiri area of Apapa, Lagos, to verify the net contents and labelling of prepackaged products, including lubricants. The inspection covered the company’s compliance with the specifications stipulated in the Eighth Schedule of the Weights and Measures Act. The team said the lubricant products examined conformed to their declared quantities, while the company pledged to obtain all relevant weight and measures certifications before the end of the year. The department said other lubricant depots, including Ardova Plc, Conoil Plc and NNPC, would be inspected during subsequent stages of the ongoing exercise. It added that the market surveillance exercise would be extended to more facilities across the country to strengthen compliance and protect consumers.
